newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan ODR increase unlikely this year-banking body.
newsitem.headline: Japan ODR increase unlikely this year-banking body.

text.p: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) is unlikely to raise its official discount rate (ODR) this year because of Japan's slow economic recovery, the new chairman of the Federation of Bankers Associations of Japan said on Wednesday.
"It would be unlikely for the BOJ to increase the discount rate within this year," Naotaka Saeki, who assumed the chairmanship last month, told Reuters in an interview.
He added, however, that it was possible that the central bank would let short-term rates rise later this year, although it was unlikely to do so anytime soon.
Saeki, also president of Sanwa Bank Ltd, said that the current trend toward firmer long-term interest rates would not be sustained because of sluggish demand for funds.
Asked about Japan's economic situation, Saeki said: "It is not deteriorating but it does not look like it is rapidly recovering."
Taking into account the impact of the consumption tax increase in April, the Japanese economy was still recovering gradually, he said.
He added, however, that corporate earnings were improving and that he expected business results for the current financial year ending next March to be better than they were last fiscal year.
He said he expected the yen to strengthen towards 115 yen against the dollar by the end of 1997 if Tokyo stock prices stabilised.

"A comfortable currency level is about 115 yen to the dollar and towards the end of this year the yen will probably strengthen toward 115 yen," he said, adding that he considered the yen's recent decline a result of worries about Japan's economic recovery.
Asked about the Tokyo stock market, Saeki said he expects the 225-share Nikkei average to consolidate around 20,000 having breached that closely watched level this week.
